title: Taxation of mutual funds
objectives: Explain how equity, debt and hybrid funds are taxed.
Know that rates change and must be verified.
body_md:
Tax depends on the fund's **equity share** and the **holding period**. Rates change often: **verify the current Finance Act before advising.**

## Classification (current framework, verify)

| Fund type | Test | Treatment |
|---|---|---|
| **Equity-oriented** | At least 65% in domestic equity | Short-term (held up to 12 months) at a special higher rate; long-term (over 12 months) at a lower rate above an annual exemption limit |
| **Specified mutual fund (debt-oriented)** | Not more than 35% in domestic equity | Gains taxed at the investor's slab rate, regardless of holding period (for purchases from April 2023) |
| **Other hybrids** | Between the two | Long-term after 24 months at a special rate; short-term at slab rate |

## Other points

- **IDCW** is taxed at the investor's slab rate; TDS applies above a threshold.
- **STT** applies on redemption of equity-oriented funds.
- **ELSS** gains follow equity rules; the deduction applies only under the old tax regime.
- **Switches** and **SWP** are redemptions and can trigger tax.
- Losses can be set off and carried forward under the Act.

> **Exam tip:** Understand the 65% and 35% tests; the exact rates change by year.
example: An investor redeems an equity fund after 14 months: long-term. After 8 months: short-term. A debt fund bought in 2024 is taxed at slab rate however long it is held.
say: Tax depends on fund type and holding period; I will confirm today's rates before you decide.
Switching funds is a sale, so tax may apply.
never: Mutual fund gains are always tax-free.
Debt funds still get indexation benefit.

check.why: At least 65% in domestic equity makes it equity-oriented for tax.
